description: Our LIMS uses a shared analyst login for the QC lab. Audit trails are turned off to improve performance.
Operators print blank batch record forms as needed from a Word template on a shared drive. Forms are not numbered or reconciled.
When a QC test result is out of specification, the analyst reruns the sample and reports the passing result. The failing result is invalidated without a documented investigation.
Chromatography data is often reprocessed with different integration parameters. Only the final processed result is kept; earlier processing versions are deleted.
For our HPLC, we keep paper printouts of the results as the official record and delete the original electronic data files after printing.
Every analyst has a unique login with role-based permissions, and system administrators are independent of the people who generate data. QA reviews audit trails for each batch before release.

Electronic records past active use are archived to microfilm with content and meaning preserved, as our predicate rules allow. During inspections we provide investigators with PDF copies of electronic records.

For our learning management system that stores training records, we documented its intended use, assessed its features as not high process risk, used unscripted ad-hoc testing, and recorded the testing results with the tester and date.

An AI model's output is the sole basis for a drug development decision. We have not defined its context of use or assessed model risk, and we do not monitor the model for performance drift after deployment.
